propositions: The reconciler's cursor advances unconditionally to the newest event in each pass, permanently dropping candidates that failed to vote (timeout, error, deferred) before the pass completed.

Gerrit webhooks deliver at-most-once (not at-least-once as documented), so dropped webhook events are lost forever unless the reconciler re-drives them—but the reconciler cannot because it skips them on the next pass.
Changes stall unvoted indefinitely after their upload event is skipped; only manual nudges (recheck-review or no-op rebase) that generate a new event with a later timestamp revive them.
The guarding test for reconciler retry was a false green because its mock ignored the since parameter, never exercising the production cursor filter behavior.

The fix introduces a low-water mark: the cursor is clamped to the minimum of newest_event and oldest_retryably_abandoned_candidate, bounded by RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS to prevent permanent pinning.
Observable state for queued, running, and dropped changes is now exposed via /health queue_depth and reconcile_done held_back/cursor fields.
